rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh gathered the sorcerers and the instruments with which he meant to plot.
rows.anchor: ما يكاد به يعني السحرة وآلاتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh then came at the appointed time.
rows.anchor: ثم أتى } الموعد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses warns them not to falsely call God's signs sorcery.
rows.anchor: بأن تدعوا آياته سحرا. { فيسحتكم بعذاب } فيهلككم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment will destroy and eradicate them.
rows.anchor: فيهلككم ويستأصلكم، وبه قرأ حمزة والكسائي

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص ويعقوب
rows.claim: They read the verb with ḍamma, from isḥāt, a Najdi and Tamimi form; suḥt is the Hijazi form.
rows.anchor: وبه قرأ حمزة والكسائي وحفص ويعقوب بالضم من الاسحات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fabricator fails, as Pharaoh did: his fabrication and scheming could not preserve his rule.
rows.anchor: كما خاب فرعون، فإنه افترى واحتال ليبقى الملك عليه فلم ينفعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sorcerers disputed about Moses; on hearing him, some said this was not a sorcerer's speech.
rows.anchor: أي تنازعت السحرة في أمر موسى حين سمعوا كلامه فقال بعضهم: ليس هذا من كلام السحرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may instead have secretly debated what to use against Moses, or Pharaoh and his people may be the subject of the pronouns.
rows.anchor: أو تنازعوا واختلفوا فيما يعارضون به موسى وتشاوروا في السر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sorcerer charge explains the secret counsel: they fabricated it lest people follow Moses and Aaron if they lost.
rows.anchor: تفسير ل { أسروا النجوى } كأنهم تشاوروا في تلفيقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis makes hādhān the subject of inna by the Banū al-Ḥārith ibn Kaʿb dual form, where alif marks the dual and case is estimated.
rows.anchor: اسم إن على لغة بلحرث بن كعب فإنهم جعلوا الألف للتثنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other parses take the subject as omitted pronoun al-shaʾn, treat in as yes, or reconstruct an omitted pronoun; Bayḍāwī objects that the lām-confirmed clause is unlikely to be omitted.
rows.anchor: وقيل اسمها ضمير الشأن المحذوف

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads an hādhayni, the straightforward accusative form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو «أن هذين» وهو ظاهر

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وحفص
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Ḥafṣ read an hādhān, taking in as lightened with the distinguishing lām, or as negative with lām meaning illa.
rows.anchor: وابن كثير وحفص { أن هذن } على أنها هي المخففة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alleged expulsion means taking control of the land.
rows.anchor: بالاستيلاء عليها. { بسحرهما ويذهبا بطريقتكم المثلى } بمذهبكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best way is their religion and doctrine, which Moses and Aaron would supplant by establishing theirs, as Pharaoh says elsewhere.
rows.anchor: بمذهبكم الذي هو أفضل المذاهب بإظهار مذهبهما وإعلاء دينهما لقوله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes the phrase as the people of your way, namely the Israelites, who were learned among them.
rows.anchor: وقيل أرادوا أهل طريقتكم وهم بنو إسرائيل فإنهم كانوا أرباب علم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further view understands ṭarīqa as the chiefs and notables, exemplary to others.
rows.anchor: وقيل الطريقة اسم لوجوه القوم وأشرافهم من حيث إنهم قدوة لغيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are told to resolve their plan together so that none holds back.
rows.anchor: فأزمعوه واجعلوه مجمعا عليه لا يتخلف عنه واحد منكم

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads fa-ajmiʿū, supported by Pharaoh's earlier gathering of plotters in 20:60.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو { فأجمعوا } ويعضده قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are to come lined up; a line makes a more imposing sight to observers.
rows.anchor: مصطفين لأنه أهيب في صدور الرائين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A report says they numbered seventy thousand, each carrying a rope and staff, and advanced all at once.
rows.anchor: قيل كانوا سبعين ألفا مع كل واحد منهم حبل عصا وأقبلوا عليه إقبالة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who prevails wins what he seeks; the clause is parenthetical.
rows.anchor: فاز بالمطلوب من غلب وهو اعتراض

words: إما أن تلقي وإما أن نكون أول من ألقى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After arriving, the sorcerers show courtesy by letting Moses choose who casts first.
rows.anchor: أي بعد ما أتوا مراعاة للأدب

words: إما أن تلقي وإما أن نكون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction may be governed by an omitted verb, or be a predicate with an omitted subject: choose your casting first or ours, or the matter is your casting or ours.
rows.anchor: و { أن } بما بعده منصوب بفعل مضمر أو مرفوع بخبرية محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses answers courtesy with courtesy and shows no concern about their magic; he lets them expend their full effort before God manifests His power and truth crushes falsehood.
rows.anchor: مقابلة أدب بأدب وعدم مبالاة بسحرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idhā is for sudden occurrence, but also has adverbial force requiring a governing verb and a following clause; here Moses is suddenly confronted with the seeming motion.
rows.anchor: وهي للمفاجأة والتحقيق أنها أيضا ظرفية تستدعي متعلقا ينصبها وجملة تضاف إليها

words: يخيل إليه من سحرهم أنها تسعى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They coated the ropes and staffs with mercury; heated by sunlight, they shook and appeared to move.
rows.anchor: بأنهم لطخوها بالزئبق فلما ضربت عليها الشمس اضطربت فخيل إليه أنها تتحرك

rows.speaker: ابن عامر برواية ابن ذكوان وروح
rows.claim: They read takhayyalu with feminine agreement referring to the ropes and staffs, with anna tasʿā as an appositional explanation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر برواية ابن ذكوان وروح «تخيل» بالتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading has the verb with yāʾ, assigning it to God; takhayyalu can also mean that they seemed to move.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { يخيل } بالياء على إسناده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will not choose Pharaoh over the truth and signs that came through Moses; the pronoun may refer to what came to us.
rows.anchor: لن نختارك. { على ما جاءنا } موسى به، ويجوز أن يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bayyināt are the clear miracles.
rows.anchor: { من البينت } المعجزات الواضحات. { والذى فطرنا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may be coordinated with what came to them or be an oath by their Creator.
rows.anchor: عطف على ما جاءنا أو قسم. { فاقض ما أنت قاض }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They tell Pharaoh to do or decree whatever he will.
rows.anchor: ما أنت قاضيه أي صانعه أو حاكم به.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh can only do what he wishes or judge as he sees fit in this life; that limits his power and prepares the contrast with the hereafter.
rows.anchor: إنما تصنع ما تهواه، أو تحكم ما تراه في هذه الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with the active form taqḍī is likened to the passive form in ṣīma yawm al-jumʿa.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { تقضي هذه الحياة الدنيا } كقولك: صيم يوم الجمعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their past sins include disbelief and other acts of disobedience.
rows.anchor: من الكفر والمعاصي. { وما أكرهتنا عليه من السحر } من معارضة المعجزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What Pharaoh forced them to do was oppose the miracle with magic.
rows.anchor: من معارضة المعجزة. روي أنهم قالوا لفرعون أرنا موسى نائما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sorcerers asked Pharaoh to show them Moses asleep; seeing his staff guard him, they judged it was not magic since a magician's power fails in sleep, but Pharaoh insisted they challenge him.
rows.anchor: روي أنهم قالوا لفرعون أرنا موسى نائما فوجدوه تحرسه العصا فقالوا ما هذا بسحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can mean God is better and more lasting in reward, or better in reward and more lasting in punishment.
rows.anchor: جزاء أو خير ثوابا وأبقى عقابا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in innahu refers to the affair or matter.
rows.anchor: { إنه } إن الأمر. { من يأت ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminal is one who dies persisting in disbelief and disobedience.
rows.anchor: بأن يموت على كفره وعصيانه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He does not die and so cannot find relief.
rows.anchor: فيستريح. { ولا يحيا } حياة مهنأة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He has no comfortable or pleasant life.
rows.anchor: فيستريح. { ولا يحيا } حياة مهنأة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gardens of Eden is an appositive for the degrees mentioned immediately before.
rows.anchor: بدل من الدرجات. { تجرى من تحتها الأنهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The abiding phrase is circumstantial; its governor is either the demonstrative's meaning or the notion of abiding there.
rows.anchor: حال والعامل فيها معنى الإشارة أو الاستقرار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purification means cleansing oneself of the stains of unbelievers and sins.
rows.anchor: تطهر من أدناس الكفار والمعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three preceding verses may be the sorcerers' words, or the beginning of God's own speech.
rows.anchor: والآيات الثلاث يحتمل أن تكون من كلام السحرة وأن تكون ابتداء كلام من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's essence and attributes transcend likeness to creatures; His speech differs from theirs as His essence differs from theirs.
rows.anchor: في ذاته وصفاته عن مماثلة المخلوقين لا يماثل كلامه كلامهم كما لا تماثل ذاته ذاتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's command and prohibition take effect, and He rightly inspires hope in His promise and fear of His threat.
rows.anchor: النافذ أمره ونهيه الحقيق بأن يرجى وعده ويخشى وعيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥaqq may mean rightful in His dominion by virtue of His essence, or true in His essence and attributes.
rows.anchor: في ملكوته يستحقه لذاته، أو الثابت في ذاته وصفاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The primary prohibition is against hastening to receive revelation from Gabriel or reciting along before he completes it; the mention of revelation follows an aside about its sending.
rows.anchor: نهي عن الاستعجال في تلقي الوحي من جبريل عليه السلام ومساوقته في القراءة حتى يتم وحيه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view prohibits conveying material stated generally before its clarification arrived.
rows.anchor: وقيل نهي عن تبليغ ما كان مجملا قبل أن يأتي بيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Instead of hastening, the Prophet asks God for more knowledge, since revelation will certainly reach him.
rows.anchor: أي سل الله زيادة العلم بدل الاستعجال فإن ما أوحى إليك تناله لا محالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's covenant to Adam was a command; عهد إليه is used for commanding and enjoining.
rows.anchor: ولقد أمرناه يقال تقدم الملك إليه وأوعز إليه وعزم عليه وعهد إليه إذا أمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic lām answers an unexpressed oath.
rows.anchor: واللام جواب قسم محذوف وإنما عطف قصة آدم على قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam's story is linked to 46:27 to show that human nature is deeply rooted in disobedience and forgetfulness.
rows.anchor: للدلالة على أن أساس بني آدم على العصيان وعرقهم راسخ في النسيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min qabl means before this time.
rows.anchor: من قبل هذا الزمان. { فنسى } العهد ولم يعن به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam either forgot and neglected the covenant or abandoned the instruction to keep away from the tree.
rows.anchor: العهد ولم يعن به حتى غفل عنه، أو ترك ما وصي به من الاحتراز عن الشجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAzm is firmness of judgment; with such resolve, Satan could not have misled Adam.
rows.anchor: تصميم رأي وثباتا على الأمر إذ لو كان ذا عزيمة وتصلب لم يزله الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bayḍāwī suggests this may have been at the beginning of Adam's life, before experience taught him hardship and ease.
rows.anchor: ولعل ذلك كان في بدء أمره قبل أن يجرب الأمور ويذوق شريها وأريها

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet reportedly said Adam's intellect would outweigh that of his descendants if they were weighed, despite this verse's statement about his resolve.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view understands ʿazm as intention to sin, since Adam erred without deliberate intent.
rows.anchor: وقيل عزما على الذنب لأنه أخطأ ولم يتعمده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If najid means know, lahu and ʿazman are its two objects; if it means find, lahu is circumstantial or governed by the verb.
rows.anchor: ونجد إن كان من الوجود الذي بمعنى العلم فله عزما مفعولاه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning means do not become a cause through which Satan brings about your expulsion.
rows.anchor: فلا يكونن سببا لإخراجكما، والمراد نهيهما عن أن يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although both are expelled, hardship is assigned to Adam because his suffering entails hers as provider, and for the verse's cadence.
rows.anchor: وأفرده بإسناد الشقاء إليه بعد إشراكهما في الخروج اكتفاء باستلزام شقائه شقاءها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively hardship means toil to earn a living, traditionally the man's task; the following verses support this reading.
rows.anchor: أو لأن المراد بالشقاء التعب في طلب المعاش وذلك وظيفة الرجال ويؤيده قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Adam is promised that in the Garden he will neither hunger nor lack clothing.
rows.anchor: إن لك أن لا تجوع فيها ولا تعرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Together with the preceding verse, this recalls the Garden's four provisions: food, drink, clothing and shelter, without effort to obtain them or fear that they will disappear.
rows.anchor: بيان وتذكير لما له في الجنة من أسباب الكفاية وأقطاب الكفاف التي هي الشبع والري والكسوة والسكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning the opposites of deprivation evokes the varieties of hardship from which Adam was warned.
rows.anchor: بذكر نقائضها، ليطرق سمعه بأصناف الشقوة المحذر عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction substitutes for anna in its syntactic function, not as the particle in itself, so its entry upon anna is permissible.
rows.anchor: والعاطف وإن ناب عن أن لكنه ناب من حيث إنه عامل لا من حيث إنه حرف تحقيق

rows.speaker: نافع وأبو بكر
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ and Abū Bakr read wa-innaka with kasra on the hamza; the other readers use fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وأبو بكر { وإنك لا تظمؤا } بكسر الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual is addressed either to Adam and Eve or to Adam and Iblis; as progenitors, Adam and Eve can be addressed in language encompassing their descendants.
rows.anchor: الخطاب لآدم وحواء، أو له ولإبليس ولما كانا أصلي الذرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hostility may arise from the contest and conflict of livelihood among people, or from each kind's condition being disrupted through the other; the following favors the first.
rows.anchor: لأمر المعاش كما عليه الناس من التجاذب والتحارب، أو لاختلال حال كل من النوعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guidance from God is a revealed book and a messenger.
rows.anchor: كتاب ورسول. { فمن اتبع هداي فلا يضل } في الدنيا. { ولا يشقى } في الآخرة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever follows God's guidance will not go astray in this world or suffer in the next.
rows.anchor: كتاب ورسول. { فمن اتبع هداي فلا يضل } في الدنيا. { ولا يشقى } في الآخرة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's remembrance here is the guidance that remembers Him and calls people to worship Him.
rows.anchor: عن الهدى الذاكر لي والداعي إلى عبادتي.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḍankan means narrow; as a verbal noun used adjectivally, it has the same form for masculine and feminine.
rows.anchor: ضيقا مصدر وصف به ولذلك يستوي فيه المذكر والمؤنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading is ḍankā, on the pattern sukrā.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { ضنكى } كسكرى، وذلك لأن مجامع همته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denier fixates on worldly goods, struggles to increase them, and fears their loss, unlike the believer who seeks the hereafter.
rows.anchor: مجامع همته ومطامح نظره تكون إلى أعراض الدنيا متهالكا على ازديادها خائفا على انتقاصها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may narrow life through unbelief and expand it through faith's blessing, as the cited verses show.
rows.anchor: كما قال وضربت عليهم الذلة والمسكنة [البقرة: 61]

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other explanations identify the constrained life with the thorny plant and zaqqūm in Hell, or with punishment in the grave.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو الضريع والزقوم في النار، وقيل عذاب القبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hāʾ may be vowelless like a pause form, or the verb jussive, coordinated with the conditional response's syntactic position.
rows.anchor: قرىء بسكون الهاء على لفظ الوقف وبالجزم عطفا على محل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person is gathered blind in physical sight or in the heart; Bayḍāwī indicates the first is supported.
rows.anchor: أعمى البصر أو القلب ويؤيد الأول

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī apply imāla to both occurrences of aʿmā because the alif derives from yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقد أمالهما حمزة والكسائي لأن الألف منقلبة من الياء

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr distinguishes the first occurrence because it is at a verse ending and pause position, which favors a change.
rows.anchor: وفرق أبو عمرو بأن الأول رأس الآية ومحل الوقف فهو جدير بالتغيير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening means that God treated the person in just that way; the verse then explains what that means.
rows.anchor: أي مثل ذلك فعلت ثم فسره فقال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetting God's clear signs means becoming blind to them and leaving them unattended.
rows.anchor: فعميت عنها وتركتها غير منظور إليها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Just as the person neglected the signs, he is now left in blindness and punishment.
rows.anchor: ومثل تركك إياها. { اليوم تنسى } تترك في العمى والعذاب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Excess means plunging into appetites and turning away from the signs.
rows.anchor: بالانهماك في الشهوات والإعراض عن الآيات.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Not believing the signs means denying them and acting against them.
rows.anchor: بل كذب بها وخالفها. { ولعذاب الأخرة } وهو الحشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hereafter's punishment may mean resurrection while blind, or the Fire that follows.
rows.anchor: وهو الحشر على العمى، وقيل عذاب النار أي وللنار بعد ذلك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is harsher and more lasting than straitened worldly life, or than that together with blindness; blindness may end in Hell so the person sees his place and condition.
rows.anchor: من ضنك العيش أو منه ومن العمى، ولعله إذا دخل النار زال عماه ليرى محله وحاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypothetical destruction could be before Muhammad, before the proof and reminder (which amount to proof), or before the Qur'an.
rows.anchor: من قبل محمد عليه الصلاة والسلام أو البينة والتذكير لأنها في معنى البرهان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They would have asked why no messenger was sent so they could follow God's signs before worldly humiliation by killing and captivity and disgrace in Hell.
rows.anchor: بالقتل والسبي في الدنيا. { ونخزى } بدخول النار يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbs for being humiliated and disgraced are also read in the passive voice.
rows.anchor: وقد قرىء بالبناء للمفعول فيهما.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each side is waiting to see what its affair will come to.
rows.anchor: أي كل واحد منا ومنكم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading is fa-tamattaʿū, so enjoy yourselves.
rows.anchor: منتظر لما يؤول إليه أمرنا وأمركم. { فتربصوا } وقرىء «فتمتعوا».

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṣirāṭ al-sawī is the straight path.
rows.anchor: المستقيم، وقرىء «السواء» أي الوسط الجيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reported readings include al-sawāʾ, the good middle; al-sūʾ, evil; and al-suwayy, a diminutive of al-sūʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «السواء» أي الوسط الجيد و «السوآى» و «السوء» أي الشر، و «السوي» هو تصغيره

words: من أصحاب الصراط السوي ومن اهتدى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both instances of man may be interrogative nominative subjects; the second may instead be relative, coordinated with the suspended interrogative clause, its subject, or the path if that means the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون الثانية موصولة بخلاف الأولى لعدم العائد فتكون معطوفة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet promises the reader of Ṭā Hā the reward of the Emigrants and Helpers on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: وعنه صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rawāsī means firm mountains, from the verb for a thing becoming fixed.
rows.anchor: ثابتات من رسا الشيء إذا ثبت.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mountains were made so the earth would not sway or shake beneath its people.
rows.anchor: كراهة أن تميل بهم وتضطرب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternate parse supplies an omitted lā to read the phrase as because it should not sway.
rows.anchor: وقيل لأن لا تميد فحذف لا لأمن الإلباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting fijājan, an adjective of subulan, makes it circumstantial and indicates the paths were broad when earth was created; alternatively, subulan replaces it, implying creation and widening for travelers with added emphasis.
rows.anchor: مسالك واسعة وإنما قدم فجاجا وهو وصف له ليصير حالا فيدل على أنه حين خلقها خلقها كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paths help people find what they need and reach their destinations.
rows.anchor: لعلهم يهتدون } إلى مصالحهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky is protected by God's power from falling, or by His will from corruption and disruption until the appointed time, or from eavesdropping through shooting stars.
rows.anchor: عن الوقوع بقدرته أو الفساد والإخلال إلى الوقت المعلوم بمشيئته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky's conditions point to the Creator's existence, oneness, power and wisdom; some are sensed, others investigated in natural philosophy and astronomy, yet people turn away without reflection.
rows.anchor: عن أحوالها الدالة على وجود الصانع ووحدته وكمال قدرته وتناهي حكمته التي يحس ببعضها

words: وهو الذي خلق الليل والنهار والشمس والقمر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The created night and day and courses of sun and moon further explain the signs just mentioned.
rows.anchor: بيان لبعض تلك الآيات. { كل فى فلك } أي كل واحد منهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each is meant; the tanwīn stands in place of a genitive complement, and falak is generic singular, like a prince clothing people in a garment.
rows.anchor: أي كل واحد منهما، والتنوين بدل من المضاف إليه والمراد بالفلك الجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They move swiftly along the orbit's surface like a swimmer moving over water.
rows.anchor: يسرعون على سطح الفلك إسراع السابح على سطح الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yasbaḥūn is the predicate of kull and the sentence circumstantial to sun and moon; plural agreement reflects multiple risings, and the rational plural pronoun is used because swimming is their action.
rows.anchor: وهو خبر { كل } والجملة حال من { الشمس والقمر } ، وجاز انفرادهما بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage was revealed when opponents said they would wait for the Prophet's death; the cited poem echoes the same idea.
rows.anchor: نزلت حين قالوا نتربص به ريب المنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fāʾ connects the condition to what precedes, and the hamza repudiates the implication after the point is established.
rows.anchor: والفاء لتعلق الشرط بما قبله والهمزة لإنكاره بعد ما تقرر ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They returned to themselves by reconsidering and regaining the use of reason.
rows.anchor: وراجعوا عقولهم. { فقالوا } فقال بعضهم لبعض.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They called themselves wrongdoers either for asking this question or for worshipping helpless idols, not for having called Abraham a wrongdoer.
rows.anchor: بهذا السؤال أو بعبادة من لا ينطق ولا يضر ولا ينفع لا من ظلمتموه بقولكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After reasoning straightened them, they returned to argument; the reversal pictures a thing's bottom rising above its top.
rows.anchor: انقلبوا إلى المجادلة بعدما استقاموا بالمراجعة، شبه عودهم إلى الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is also read with doubled kāf or as transitive, meaning they turned themselves upside down.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { نكسوا } بالتشديد و { نكسوا } أي نكسوا أنفسهم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their reply means Abraham knew the idols could not speak, so why had he told them to ask them? The wording presumes an unspoken question.
rows.anchor: فكيف تأمرنا بسؤالها وهو على إرادة القول.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham rebukes worship of things that cannot benefit or harm, contradicting their admission that the idols are inert.
rows.anchor: إنكار لعبادتهم لها بعد اعترافهم بأنها جمادات لا تنفع ولا تضر فإنه ينافي الألوهية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Uff is an exclamation of exasperation meaning something vile and foul; the lām identifies the object of disgust.
rows.anchor: تضجر منه على إصرارهم بالباطل البين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question rebukes them for failing to understand how abhorrent their practice is.
rows.anchor: اللام لبيان المتأفف له. { أفلا تعقلون } قبح صنيعكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhu al-Nūn, the companion of the whale, is Jonah son of Mattā.
rows.anchor: وصاحب الحوت يونس بن متى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Frustrated by prolonged resistance, Jonah left before being commanded or before the threatened punishment was due; the people repented, but he did not know and thought they had deceived him.
rows.anchor: لما برم بطول دعوتهم وشدة شكيمتهم وتمادي إصرارهم مهاجرا عنهم، قبل أن يؤمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form may intensify anger, or mean he angered his people by leaving, since they feared punishment would follow.
rows.anchor: وهو من بناء المغالبة للمبالغة أو لأنه أغضبهم بالمهاجرة لخوفهم لحوق العذاب عندها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading is maghḍaban.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «مغضبا». { فظن أن لن نقدر عليه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may mean God would not constrict Jonah or decree punishment for him; an intensive reading supports the latter.
rows.anchor: لن نضيق عليه أو لن نقضي عليه بالعقوبة من القدر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view treats it as a comparison to one who thinks he can flee God's decree by leaving without waiting for God's order, or as a fleeting satanic thought hyperbolically called a supposition.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو تمثيل لحاله بحال من ظن أن لن نقدر عليه في مراغمته قومه

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Other readings use yāʾ, a passive construction by Yaʿqūb, and a doubled consonant in that form.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالياء وقرأ يعقوب على البناء للمفعول وقرىء به مثقلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The darkness may be exceptionally dense, or the three dark places of the whale's belly, sea and night.
rows.anchor: في الظلمة الشديدة المتكاثفة أو ظلمات بطن الحوت والبحر والليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah confesses that none but God is divine.
rows.anchor: بأنه لا إله إلا أنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is exalted above any incapacity; nothing can defeat Him.
rows.anchor: سبحنك } من أن يعجزك شيء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jonah wronged himself by leaving hastily before receiving God's command.
rows.anchor: بالمبادرة إلى المهاجرة. وعن النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام
rows.claim: The Prophet says no distressed person who invokes God with this supplication fails to have it answered.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zabūr here is David's book.
rows.anchor: في كتاب داود عليه السلام.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-dhikr may be the Torah; alternatively, Zabūr means revealed books generally and al-dhikr the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: أي التوراة، وقيل المراد ب { الزبور } جنس الكتب المنزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth to be inherited may be the Garden or the Holy Land.
rows.anchor: أي أرض الجنة أو الأرض المقدسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous heirs may mean all believers, the formerly oppressed who inherit the world's east and west, or Muhammad's community.
rows.anchor: يعني عامة المؤمنين أو الذين كانوا يستضعفون مشارق الأرض ومغاربها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative stands for an omitted clause, meaning the matter is so; similar wording separates two stretches of discourse.
rows.anchor: خبر محذوف أي الأمر ذلك وهو وأمثاله تطلق للفصل بين كلامين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's inviolate things may mean His rulings and all that must not be violated, or the sanctuary and pilgrimage obligations.
rows.anchor: أحكامه وسائر ما لا يحل هتكه، أو الحرم وما يتعلق بالحج من التكاليف.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A narrower view identifies the inviolate things as the Kaaba, Sacred Mosque, sacred territory, sacred month and pilgrim in consecration.
rows.anchor: وقيل الكعبة والمسجد الحرام والبلد الحرام والشهر الحرام والمحرم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reverence is better for the person as a reward with his Lord.
rows.anchor: { فهو خير له } فالتعظيم { خير له }.

words: وأحلت لكم الأنعام إلا ما يتلى عليكم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Livestock are lawful except what God declared forbidden for an incidental reason, such as carrion or an animal offered to other than God; do not invent bans such as baḥīra and sāʾiba.
rows.anchor: إلا المتلو عليكم تحريمه، وهو ما حرم منها لعارض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling idols impurity to be shunned like filth strongly intensifies the prohibition of revering or worshipping them.
rows.anchor: اجتنبوا الرجس الذي هو الأوثان كما تجتنب الأنجاس، وهو غاية المبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Avoiding false speech generalizes after the specific prohibition because idol worship is the chief falsehood; the context rebukes pagan practices and false claims about God's law.
rows.anchor: تعميم بعد تخصيص فإن عبادة الأوثان رأس الزور، كأنه لما حث على تعظيم الحرمات أتبعه ذلك ردا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes this as false testimony, supported by a Prophetic report equating it with associating partners with God and reciting this verse.
rows.anchor: وقيل شهادة الزور لما روي

rows.speaker: النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام
rows.claim: The Prophet said false testimony is equivalent to associating partners with God, repeating the comparison three times, then recited this verse.
rows.anchor: روي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zūr derives from deviation, as ifk derives from turning away; a lie departs from reality.
rows.anchor: من الزور وهو الانحراف كما أن الإفك من الأفك وهو الصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra is Meccan; it has 119 verses according to the Basrans and 118 according to the Kufans.
rows.anchor: مكية وهي مائة وتسع عشرة آية عند البصريين وثماني عشرة عند الكوفيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qad affirms an expected outcome, as lamā negates one while indicating its settled occurrence with the past; it brings that past near the present, fitting believers' expectation of God's bounty and their glad tidings.
rows.anchor: قد تثبت المتوقع كما أن لما تنفيه وتدل على ثباته إذا دخلت على الماضي

rows.speaker: ورش عن نافع
rows.claim: Warsh from Nāfiʿ transfers the hamza's vowel to the dāl and deletes the hamza.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ورش عن نافع { قد أفلح } بإلقاء حركة الهمزة على الدال وحذفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading uses plural aflaḥū by dialect or anticipatory subject clarified afterward; other forms use ḍamma instead of wāw or the passive.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «أفلحوا» على لغة: أكلوني البراغيث، أو على الإبهام والتفسير، و { أفلح } بالضم اجتزاء بالضمة عن الواو و «أفلح» على البناء للمفعول.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khushūʿ is reverent fear and humility before God, with the gaze held at the place of prostration.
rows.anchor: خائفون من الله سبحانه وتعالى متذللون له ملزمون أبصارهم مساجدهم

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet used to pray looking toward the sky; after this verse was revealed, he turned his gaze toward his place of prostration.
rows.anchor: روي أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يصلي رافعا بصره إلى السماء، فلما نزلت رمى ببصره نحو مسجده

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Seeing a man play with his beard, the Prophet said that if his heart were humble, his limbs would be humble too.
rows.anchor: روي أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يصلي رافعا بصره إلى السماء، فلما نزلت رمى ببصره نحو مسجده وأنه رأى رجلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following bodily worship with financial worship shows they reach the utmost in religious duties and avoidance of forbidden and unbecoming things.
rows.anchor: وصفهم بذلك بعد وصفهم بالخشوع في الصلاة ليدل على أنهم بلغوا الغاية في القيام على الطاعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zakāt may denote the abstract duty, since an agent performs the event rather than its object; or the material after ellipsis of a genitive noun.
rows.anchor: والزكاة تقع على المعنى والعين والمواد الأول لأن الفاعل فاعل الحدث لا المحل الذي هو موقعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beyond that means beyond what was excepted as licit.
rows.anchor: المستثنى. { فأولئك هم العادون } الكاملون في العدوان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such people are fully given to transgression.
rows.anchor: الكاملون في العدوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their trusts and covenants include what is entrusted or promised on behalf of God or people; they preserve and set them right.
rows.anchor: لما يؤتمنون عليه ويعاهدون من جهة الحق أو الخلق.

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr reads singular amānah here and in al-Maʿārij, either to avoid ambiguity or because the singular is the original verbal noun.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير هنا وفي «المعارج» { لأمانتهم } على الإفراد ولأمن الإلباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They keep up prayer by performing it regularly and at its appointed times.
rows.anchor: يواظبون عليها ويؤدونها في أوقاتها، ولفظ الفعل فيه لما في الصلاة من التجدد والتكرر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular form reflects prayer's renewal and repetition; most readers use the plural except Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī.
rows.anchor: ولفظ الفعل فيه لما في الصلاة من التجدد والتكرر ولذلك جمعه غير حمزة والكسائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is not redundant with the opening quality: humility differs from guarding prayer, and framing the traits with prayer honors its rank.
rows.anchor: وليس ذلك تكريرا لما وصفهم به أولا فإن الخشوع في الصلاة غير المحافظة عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who combine all these traits alone deserve to be called inheritors.
rows.anchor: الأحقاء بأن يسموا وراثا دون غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The later generation may be the people of ʿĀd or Thamūd.
rows.anchor: هم عاد أو ثمود.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger from among them may be Hūd or Ṣāliḥ.
rows.anchor: هو هود أو صالح، وإنما جعل القول موضع الإرسال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting the messenger's speech in place of the sending indicates he was not brought from elsewhere; revelation came while he lived among them.
rows.anchor: وإنما جعل القول موضع الإرسال ليدل على أنه لم يأتهم من مكان غير مكانهم وإنما أوحي إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to worship explains the sending: God told them through the messenger to worship Him alone and fear His punishment.
rows.anchor: { أن اعبدوا الله ما لكم من إله غيره } تفسير لأرسلنا أي قلنا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wāw may signal that their speech did not directly follow the messenger's speech, unlike the renewed speech of Noah's people; the explanation assumes a question.
rows.anchor: لعله ذكر بالواو لأن كلامهم لم يتصل بكلام الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They denied either the reward and punishment of the hereafter or resurrection into a second life.
rows.anchor: بلقاء ما فيها من الثواب والعقاب، أو بمعادهم إلى الحياة الثانية بالبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were made luxurious through abundant wealth and children.
rows.anchor: ونعمناهم { في الحياة الدنيا } بكثرة الأموال والأولاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The notables insist the messenger shares their human nature and condition; his eating and drinking as they do reinforces that likeness.
rows.anchor: في الصفة والحالة. { يأكل مما تأكلون منه ويشرب مما تشربون

words: يأكل مما تأكلون منه ويشرب مما تشربون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated mā is relative; its link in the second clause is omitted, either as an accusative pronoun or with its preposition understood from the first.
rows.anchor: تقرير للمماثلة و «ما» خبرية والعائد إلى الثاني منصوب محذوف أو مجرور حذف مع الجار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chiefs claim that obeying a human like themselves would make the people losers by subjecting themselves to him.
rows.anchor: { ولئن أطعتم بشرا مثلكم } فيما يأمركم به.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idhā is the consequence of the conditional, and the clause answers the people disputing with the chiefs.
rows.anchor: حيث أذللتم أنفسكم، و { إذا } جزاء للشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They picture bodies reduced to earth and bones stripped of flesh and sinews.
rows.anchor: مجردة عن اللحوم والأعصاب. { أنكم مخرجون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being brought out may mean resurrection from graves or being recreated from nonexistence into existence.
rows.anchor: من الأجداث أو من العدم تارة أخرى إلى الوجود،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated anna may reinforce the first after a long separation from its predicate; other parses make the second a new subject with an advanced predicate, conditional answer, or clause explaining the first.
rows.anchor: و { أنكم } تكرير للأول أكد به لما طال الفصل بينه وبين خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hihaāt expresses remoteness of belief or truth.
rows.anchor: بعد التصديق أو الصحة. { لما توعدون }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām may mean for what is promised or explain it as in 12:23; they exclaim hihaāt, then identify what they dismiss.
rows.anchor: واللام للبيان كما في هيت لك

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively hihaāt itself means remoteness and is a subject whose predicate is what is promised.
rows.anchor: وقيل { هيهات } بمعنى البعد، وهو مبتدأ خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word is read with fatḥa, ḍamma or kasra, with or without tanwīn; other forms pause on sukūn or replace tāʾ with hāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالفتح منونا للتنكير، وبالضم منونا على أنه جمع هيهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The underlying phrasing was inna al-ḥayāta illā ḥayātunā al-dunyā; the pronoun replaces the first life to avoid repetition and signal its identity is self-evident.
rows.anchor: أصله إن الحياة { إلا حياتنا الدنيا } فأقيم الضمير مقام الأولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They claim no life exists beyond this world; the negative in applies to hiyā, which signifies life as a genus and has the force of lā negating a genus.
rows.anchor: ومعناه لا حياة إلا هذه الحياة لأن { إن } نافية دخلت على { هي } التي في معنى الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some people die while others are born.
rows.anchor: يموت بعضنا ويولد بعض. { وما نحن بمبعوثين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The line هي النفس ما حملتها تتحمل is cited as poetic evidence for replacing the first noun with a pronoun to avoid repetition.
rows.anchor: كقوله: هي النفس ما حملتها تتحمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They deny resurrection after death.
rows.anchor: { وما نحن بمبعوثين } بعد الموت.
